text.p: Tourist arrivals for September dropped by 5,750, or 4.7 per cent, to 115,557, figures released on Tuesday by Malta's Central Office of Statistics show.
The comparable arrivals figure for September 1995 was 121,307.

The British market, Malta's largest by far, saw a sharp decline of 8,758, or 16.2 per cent to 45,305 from 54,063 in September last year. There were also fewer French tourists, down by 1,411 to 5,727, and fewer Belgians and other nationalities.
But more tourists came from, among others, Germany, up by 1,300, Libya, up by 1,206, and Holland, up by 1,087.

The overall drop for the first nine months of 1996 was 55,386, or 6.1 per cent. Malta received a total of 846,293 visitors up to the end of September, compared to 901,679 in the comparable period last year.

Tourism income in the first nine months was Lm171.4 ($480) million, compared to Lm179.9 million ($503.7) in the same period last year. On a per capita basis, tourism earnings in the first nine months amounted to Lm202.5 ($565) this year from Lm199.5 ($557) in 1995.
